thirtySeconds: KeithK75 took the Copperhead PLAYOFF in the only number that matters around here: net. His +1 edged HamSammich's +2 by one shot, with IUDoc92 next at +7. The raw scoreboard was even more decisive, as Keith also posted the gross win at +1, ten clear of Dan94. The separator was a ridiculous +18.63 strokes gained, powered by tee-to-green work (+15.72) and positive numbers in every category. Dan's +8.63 SG total produced the second-best gross round, while Ham's +3.63 and a 15-shot net adjustment kept him in the fight despite five bogeys, three doubles, and zero birdies.
latestTournamentTeaser: KeithK75 won the Copperhead PLAYOFF at +1 net—and did it outright in gross, too. Behind him, HamSammich's adjusted +2 survived a round with three doubles, while Dan94's +11 gross was built on elite driving and a short-game rescue mission.

carnage.name: Leroy4522
carnage.commentary: Hole 12 was a full-swing hostage situation: pinestraw off the tee, rough from 74 yards, another rough miss from 21 yards, then sand from 102. Nine shots later, a 9-footer was still four feet away, leaving a gross 9 and net 8. That hole had more recovery attempts than actual recovery.

carnage.name: MashedBROtato
carnage.commentary: The par-3 eighth became an eight-piece combo. The tee shot found sand, the next two shots stayed in or beside sand, and a fourth shot finally wandered into rough. From there came a 19-yard pitch to 10 feet, a 23-footer left 13 feet away, and another putt left one foot. The tap-in was less a finish than an evacuation.

carnage.name: CRANK
carnage.commentary: CRANK's eighth was a scenic tour of Copperhead's least helpful surfaces: rough, pinestraw, fairway, semirough, then green. After taking six shots to reach 17 feet, the 15-footer missed by three feet and the tap-in closed out an eight. The approach game was already down 3.85 strokes; Hole 12 brought receipts.

carnage.name: DREADFUL
carnage.commentary: On the par-5 11th, DREADFUL needed two shots just to get from rough to pinestraw and then kept the adventure alive with rough, rough, and green. A 32-footer became an 8-footer, a 15-footer became a 7-footer, and a 6-footer became a 1-footer. Nine gross, eight net: a five-hole-length traffic jam on one hole.

carnage.name: HamSammich
carnage.commentary: The par-5 fifth started perfectly enough with fairway, then immediately filed for witness protection: rough from 179, rough from 142, rough from 83, and rough again from 27. After finally reaching six yards, Ham left a 19-footer one foot short and took the gimmie for an eight gross, seven net. That is three over on a par five with no birdie anywhere in the round.

carnage.name: IUDoc92
carnage.commentary: IUDoc92's par-3 eighth required a 127-yard tee shot to rough, a 40-yard recovery to more rough, and a 32-yard recovery to—sure enough—rough again. The green finally appeared after 13 more yards, but the 16-footer stopped three feet short. A six gross, five net, with five sand-save attempts elsewhere explaining why the short game posted -4.76 SG.

carnage.name: Dan94
carnage.commentary: Dan94's seventh was supposed to be a par 4 and instead became a sand-based miniseries: 287 yards to sand, 41 yards to sand, then one yard to sand. He eventually escaped to 19 yards, hit it to 25 feet, and two putts later had a six. The driving was worth +6.43 SG, but Hole 7 made sure the rescue crew stayed busy.

carnage.name: KeithK75
carnage.commentary: Keith's worst hole was a five, which tells you how unfairly clean this round was. Hole 16 began in rough, followed by a shot that went exactly zero yards, then a 179-yard blast to semirough and an eight-yard pitch to one foot. Tap-in five. Even the disaster had a controlled landing, and his +18.63 SG total says the rest of the course got no such mercy.

players.name: KeithK75
players.body: KeithK75 won both competitions, taking the net title at +1 and the gross title at +1 with no adjustment. He was not merely tidy; he gained 18.63 strokes overall, including 4.96 off the tee, 6.28 on approach, 4.49 around the green, and 2.91 putting. Nine greens, 27 putts, two birdies, three bogeys, and no doubles made this the rare simulator round where the scorecard does not look like it needs legal representation. His worst hole was a five on 16 after a zero-yard second shot, but he followed that with a 179-yard recovery to semirough and a one-foot pitch. He also made birdie on the par-3 eighth from 11 feet and on the par-5 fifth from 12, which is how you turn Copperhead into a personal range session.

players.name: HamSammich
players.body: HamSammich finished at +2 net, one shot behind Keith, with a 15-shot adjustment doing serious labor against a +17 gross round. The raw golf was a messy blend: +3.63 SG overall, positive off the tee (+1.76), around the green (+0.35), and with the putter (+2.77), but -1.24 on approach. Four greens in regulation, four fairways, five bogeys, and three doubles left plenty of wreckage, though the adjustment kept the net card alive. Hole 5 captured the round: five straight trips through rough or near-rough before a 12-yard pitch and a 19-footer left one foot short for an eight gross, seven net. He also managed net birdies on the first and 11th, turning survival into a legitimate net challenge.

players.name: IUDoc92
players.body: IUDoc92 posted +7 net after a +24 gross round and a 17-shot adjustment, landing third in the net race. The approach number was genuinely useful at +2.10 SG, but the rest of the game fought back hard: -0.84 tee, -4.76 short game, -0.87 putting, and -4.37 total. Three greens, 32 putts, two three-putts, nine bogeys, and three doubles explain the scorecard's general mood. On Hole 8, a 127-yard tee shot to rough was followed by two more rough recoveries before reaching the green; a 16-footer stopped three feet away for a six gross, five net. The round did include net birdies on six and 10, including a made 14-footer on 10, but the short game kept charging interest.

players.name: DREADFUL
players.body: DREADFUL's +9 net came from a +27 gross round with an 18-shot adjustment, good enough to stay in the net chase despite a -7.37 SG total. Every major department was underwater: -2.66 tee, -2.06 approach, -0.16 short game, and -2.49 putting. Two fairways, three greens, 35 putts, and four three-putts made the course feel substantially larger than the data claims it is. The par-5 11th was the centerpiece of the carnage: rough to pinestraw, then rough again, followed by a 24-foot putt that became eight feet, then seven, then one. A gross 9, net 8. Somehow, a 44-foot hole-out birdie on 15 and a made 17-footer on 7 were still hiding in the round.

players.name: CRANK
players.body: CRANK finished +10 net from +22 gross with a 12-shot adjustment, while the underlying numbers showed a round held together by short game alone. The 3.28 short-game SG was excellent, but approach lost 3.85, putting lost 1.25, and total SG settled at -2.37. Seven fairways sounds responsible; one green in regulation sounds like the greens had a restraining order. Hole 12 delivered an eight gross, seven net after rough and pinestraw visits, a 150-yard shot to fairway, and a slow march from 36 yards to 17 feet. The counterpunch was spectacular: a par-5 11 hole-out from five yards for a gross 4, plus a net birdie on that hole. Golf is apparently allowed to contain both this and that.

players.name: Dan94
players.body: Dan94 had the second-best gross result at +11 and the second-best raw SG total among the field at +8.63, but with no net adjustment that translated directly to +11 net. The engine of the round was tee play at +6.43 SG, backed by +3.10 short game and +1.22 putting, while approach gave back 2.12. He hit only three greens and four fairways, yet the long game kept producing chances, including a gross birdie on the par-5 first after a 292-yard drive and a made 8-footer. Hole 7 showed the leak: 287 yards to sand, 41 more to sand, then one yard still in sand before a 25-footer and a tap-in six. Strong raw golf, plenty of sand, and a net result that could not benefit from the adjustment math.

players.name: MashedBROtato
players.body: MashedBROtato ended at +13 net from +25 gross with a 12-shot adjustment. Tee play (+1.81) and approach (+0.90) were at least functional, but -6.00 short-game SG and -2.08 putting dragged the round into the weeds. Zero fairways, four greens, 34 putts, two three-putts, six bogeys, and four doubles made the margin for error microscopic. Hole 8 erased whatever margin existed: the 167-yard tee shot found sand, the next two shots stayed at the beach, and the fourth moved only two yards to rough before a 19-yard pitch. The 23-footer then finished 13 feet away, and the next putt stopped one foot short for an eight on a par 3. There were still net birdies on 14 and 2, including a made 6-footer on 2, but the round spent too much time negotiating with sand.

players.name: Leroy4522
players.body: Leroy4522 closed at +17 net from +29 gross with a 12-shot adjustment and the field's lowest SG total at -9.37. The damage was broad: -3.73 tee, -3.13 approach, -0.86 short game, and -1.65 putting, adding up to -7.72 tee-to-green. Two fairways, two greens, 32 putts, two three-putts, four bogeys, and four doubles left very little insulation. Hole 12 was the full audit: pinestraw from 175 yards, rough from 74, rough again from 21, sand from 102, then a 24-yard pitch to nine feet and a 14-footer left four feet short. The result was a gross 9, net 8. A gross birdie-free round still had clean moments, including a gross 4 and net 3 on the second, but Copperhead collected the rest.

stateOfLeague: Week 6 says the net race can turn on adjustment math, but KeithK75 made that argument irrelevant by winning gross and net with the field's best SG performance. The event also exposed the league's current tax bracket: one bad hole can become a full simulator incident when recovery shots and putting both join the revolt.
